analysis.title: Americas Utilities: Power - Early views on key state election results for power/utilities; potential risk to TX exposed stocks including NRG/VST
key_insights: GS focuses on four state elections (TX, GA, OH, CA) for their effect on data center development, power demand growth, pricing, utility investment and wildfire liability reform.
Democratic wins could raise near-term uncertainty around data center development, particularly in Texas and Georgia. GS still sees both as important long-term load growth markets.

Texas: Gina Hinojosa (D) beat Governor Greg Abbott (R). She has called for a data center moratorium until the legislature adds protections in 2027. GS sees this mainly as a risk to the timing of development, not the long-term opportunity.

Texas exposure: GS sees Buy-rated SRE, XEL, NRG and VST and Neutral-rated CEG and AEP as most exposed. The risk is to the timing of the load growth inflection, which could affect ERCOT power prices and regulated utility capex. GS next looks to the data center audit study due by December 10.

Georgia: Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) won the governor's race, and Democrats Peter Hubbard and Shelia Edwards won PSC seats. The Commission flips to a Democratic majority. Edwards has previously supported a data center moratorium in Georgia.

Georgia exposure: Neutral-rated SO is most exposed, with 56% of its rate base in the state. GS sees the results as potentially negative for its 75 GW+ prospective large load pipeline and broader infrastructure investment.

Ohio: Amy Acton (D) beat Vivek Ramaswamy (R). GS expects about 8 GW of data centers online in Ohio by 2030 and sees the result as slightly increasing uncertainty, with possibly stricter requirements for data centers coming online. Buy-rated FE and Neutral-rated AEP are seen as less well placed, with more limited impact on Buy-rated DUK.

California: Xavier Becerra (D) won the governor's race. Governor Newsom can still call a special legislative session on wildfire liability reform before November 15th, otherwise the decision passes to the new administration. If called, GS sees a possible positive for Buy-rated PCG and SRE and Neutral-rated EIX.
GS notes the analysis covers state results only and that federal election results could also have implications for the sector.

sector_views.rationale: Democratic wins in TX, GA and OH raise near-term uncertainty on data center development timing, but GS keeps a long-term view of these as key load growth markets.

risk_factors: Moratoria or stricter conditions on data center interconnection in Texas, Georgia and Ohio could delay the load growth inflection.
Lower-than-anticipated power prices and PJM capacity auction uncertainty are cited as downside risks for VST and NRG.
Adverse regulatory decisions on data center tariffs in Texas or Ohio are cited as a risk for AEP.
Wildfire liability reform could slip to the new California administration with unclear timing and scope.
Federal election results could carry additional implications not covered in this note.

geopolitical: Texas governor: Gina Hinojosa (D) defeated incumbent Greg Abbott (R), flipping the state from Republican to Democratic.
Georgia: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governorship and Democrats took the majority of the Public Service Commission.
Ohio: Democrat Amy Acton defeated Vivek Ramaswamy (R) for governor.
California: Xavier Becerra (D) won the governorship, and Governor Newsom's possible special session on wildfire liability reform before November 15th remains open.

tension_points.bull_case: Texas remains a long-term key data center market, and the election mainly affects the timing of development, not the long-term opportunity.
tension_points.bear_case: Hinojosa has called for a moratorium until the legislature adds protections in 2027, which could delay the load growth inflection, hitting ERCOT power prices and regulated utility capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The results of the Texas data center audit study due by December 10 are the next checkpoint GS names for the policy direction.

tension_points.bull_case: Governor-elect Becerra has said there is more work to do on wildfire policy, so reform is still a priority, and a special session could be a positive for PCG, SRE and EIX.
tension_points.bear_case: If Newsom does not call a special session, decisions go to the new administration and the timing and scope of reform are unclear.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No special legislative session being called before November 15th would remove the near-term catalyst.
